question: A large urn contains \(100\) balls, of which \(36\%\) are red and the rest are blue. How many of the blue balls must be removed so that the percentage of red balls in the urn will be \(72\%?\) (No red balls are to be removed.)
solution:
Removing blue balls keeps the red count fixed at \(0.36\cdot100=36\). For these \(36\) red balls to make up \(72\%\) of the remaining balls, the total must be
\[
\frac{36}{0.72}=50.
\]
Therefore, \(100-50=\boxed{50}\) blue balls must be removed, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
